chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: McRae's staff-writer contract with Robbins Music
summary: The Robbins deal was an advance against royalties of a thousand dollars, rising to five and ten thousand yearly.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: People who worked for Robbins and you were on the staff, were you on a commission or was it a salary position --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
A deal where they would give you like -- When I first was writing for Robbins, they gave me like a thousand dollars.
And this was supposed to cover how many songs over a certain period?

This was to (inaudible) cover any amount of songs. Just was an advance of a thousand dollars. You know, (inaudible) in the 40's -- In those days, somebody give you a thousand dollars, that was a lot of money. You're talking about in the 40's and the 30's. 40's now, right? Nobody was passing a --

-- thousand dollars around for songs, you know. So, I had a contract with a thousand dollars. (Every (inaudible)) so many weeks, so many months, like a graduating contract. You know, like a thousand dollars advance. It was five thousand dollars guaranteed a
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
year. Ten thousand dollars for the second year. This was advance money against anything you wrote. This wasn't any payment. This was against your royalties.
So he give me about a thousand dollars against -- (inaudible). I think they give everybody --

I think they gave Bud Green a thousand dollars, somebody getting two. Might give Ella a thousand dollars, (inaudible) Chick a thousand. I don't know, it was about So, (inaudible) five thousand dollars I know I (inaudible) got two thousand. The rest of them got a thousand.
Then when I came back as a writer, he signed me on as a staff writer for the company. He gave me like five thousand dollars.
The second year would be like ten thousand. That's against royalties.
